meta_desc: Energy Adventure 2 — GCSE Physics calculations for kinetic energy, gravitational potential energy, and work done.

concepts.def: Kinetic, gravitational, elastic, thermal, chemical, etc.
Energy moved between stores mechanically, electrically, by heating or radiation.
Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred.
Useful energy out ÷ total energy in (always less than 100%).
Energy transferred when a force moves an object; W = Fd.
The rate of energy transfer (watts); P = E ÷ t.

walkthroughs.body_html:
KE = ½ × m × v²

Mass in kg, speed in m/s, energy in J.

Double the speed → four times the kinetic energy, because v is squared. That's why fast cars need long stopping distances.

GPE = m × g × h 🪂

Lift a mass m to height h and you store mgh joules in its gravitational store. Use g = 9.8 N/kg (some exam boards use 10).

Example: lift a 2 kg book by 1 m → GPE = 2 × 9.8 × 1 ≈ 19.6 J.

W = F × d

Work done equals force (in N) times distance moved (in m). Work done is energy transferred — both measured in joules.

If a 10 N force pushes a box 3 m, the work done is 30 J.

mcqs.q: If you double the speed of a moving car, its kinetic energy becomes…
options: Half
The same
Doubled
Four times bigger

mcqs.q: Which equation gives the work done by a constant force?
options: W = F ÷ d
W = F × d
W = m × g × h
W = ½mv²

mcqs.q: If a car doubles its speed, what happens to its kinetic energy?
options: It quadruples (because KE = 1/2 mv^2 — kinetic energy is proportional to v^2).
Kinetic energy stays the same because mass hasn't changed.
Energy has been converted into mass following E=mc^2.
Kinetic energy doubles because energy is proportional to speed.

mcqs.q: When energy is 'lost' as heat due to friction, what has really happened?
options: Kinetic energy stays the same because mass hasn't changed.
Energy has been transferred to the thermal store of the surroundings — it's not destroyed, just dissipated.
Energy has been converted into mass following E=mc^2.
Energy has been used up and no longer exists.

mcqs.q: Can a device ever be 100 percent efficient?
options: A well-designed device can be 100 percent efficient by eliminating all friction.
Energy has been converted into mass following E=mc^2.
Efficiency above 100 percent is possible if the device extracts ambient energy.
In practice, no — some energy is always transferred to less useful stores (e.g. heat to surroundings).
